parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by radioactive decay.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A radioactive sample consists of an isotope *X* of half-life *T* that decays to form a stable product. Only *X* and the stable product are present in the sample.

At time *t* = 0, the sample has an activity of *A*₀ and contains *N*₀ nuclei of *X*.
parts.text:
On Fig. 10.1, sketch the variation with *t* of the number *N* of nuclei of *X* present in the sample. Your line should extend from time *t* = 0 to time *t* = 3*T*.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 10.2, sketch the variation with *N* of the activity *A* of the sample for values of *N* between *N* = 0 and *N* = *N*₀.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: State the name of the quantity represented by the gradient of your line in:

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: For the sample in (b), calculate the fraction $\frac{N}{N_0}$ at time *t* = 1.70*T*.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.1
figures.alt: A blank grid for sketching the number of nuclei N against time t, with time marked from 0 to 3T.

figures.caption: Fig. 10.2
figures.alt: A blank grid for sketching activity A against the number of nuclei N, with axes ranging from 0 to A₀ and from 0 to N₀.
